main_text.p: [?]t in præsenti negotio, qui promittit liquid quasi revera futurum, assumpto n veritatis confirmationem Dei nomine, quod tamen totum abit in nihil, aut on intento aut non præstito quod promissum est: is directe & ad literam assumit Dei nomen in vanum, violat præceptum Dei, & gravissimi criminis (peririi) reus est. Atque ita sat confirmatum habetis primam Hypothesin, de Juramenti Simplicitate.
main_text.head: SECT. VIII.
main_text.p: Secunda sequitur, huic cognata: quæ l Juramenti justam interpretationem ertinet; eftque breviter hæc, Juramenti obligatio est stricti juris. Jus strictum hic intelligo, non ea significatione ia fæpissime occurrit apud Jurisconsultos, pro illo rigore juris quod ἀκριβοδί-ὡν vocant, & apponitur τῷ ἐπιεικεῖ five Æquitati: quo sc. convertitur judicium in absynthium, quodque est ita im injuria fere conjunctum, ut pene in proverbium abierit illud, Summum jus summa injuria. Sed mitius aliquanto, ro interpretatione juris ita justa & suis ncellis circumscripta, ut non trahantur verbaAmos 6. 12.

page.notes: Left edge of the scan is cut off, so the first letters of several lines are missing or partly visible; these are marked [?] where uncertain. The Greek words (ἀκριβοδίκαιον hyphenated line-end, τῷ ἐπιεικεῖ) are uncertain and copied from the visible shapes. The marginal reference is printed as "Amos 6." with "12," on the following line. The final line "verba" is the last line of the page, not a catchword.
